transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for having me. Um, I hope I'm explaining this right, but... I guess I came in because I've started doing some things at work—I'm a bookkeeping clerk—and at school that... well, I guess they don't make a whole lot of sense. 

It's nothing terrible, really! Just some little quirks, I think. Like, I've been lining business receipts all across the floor. And I'll catch myself tapping the calculator in sets of nine. I know it sounds a little strange... is this the kind of thing you need to know? 

I've also, um... I've been standing by the copier sometimes, just... with my hands held up in the air, waiting until someone asks if I'm okay. I feel a little embarrassed even saying it out loud, to be honest. I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in to talk about it. Am I in the right place for this?
Do these behaviors bother you or cause you any anxiety, or do they feel like something you just naturally want to do?

Um, well... they don't really bother me, exactly. It's not like I'm anxious or scared if I don't do them. It just... I don't know, it just feels like the right thing to do at the time, I guess? Like it's just a natural little habit. 

I mean, I know it looks weird to other people, which is why I feel bad if it disrupts anyone at work. I definitely don't want to cause any trouble for my boss or my coworkers. But for me, inside... it's just something I do. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right. I just don't want to make a bigger deal out of it than it actually is.
Have these behaviors ever caused you any distress, or made it hard for you to function at work or school?

Well, um... I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or making excuses, because I know I just need to try harder. But... I guess it has made things a little tricky lately. 

Like, at school, I did end up failing one of my important course modules. I'm sure I can make it up, though! And at work... well, my boss pointed out that some of my ledgers have been coming back with some, um, pretty serious errors. I've actually had to ask my coworkers for help finishing up some of the routine stuff that I usually do on my own. I feel terrible about bothering them. 

I just... I want to be doing a good job, you know? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just being lazy or careless. Is it okay that I'm struggling with this a little bit right now?
Do you ever feel like these behaviors are meant to prevent something bad from happening, or to reduce some kind of worry or discomfort that you're feeling?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. It's definitely not like I'm trying to stop a disaster or anything like that. I promise I'm not overly anxious or, you know, secretly terrified of something bad happening. 

It's really just... I just do it. There's no worry or discomfort that I'm trying to make go away. I hope I didn't make it sound like I was hiding some big fear from you! I really try to stay pretty positive overall. Is it... is it a good thing that it's not coming from a place of worry? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have you noticed any unwanted or intrusive thoughts that come into your mind, even if you don’t act on them?

Um, no, not really. I mean, everybody has weird little thoughts sometimes, right? But nothing that really bothers me or gets stuck in my head. I try to keep my mind focused on, you know, good things and getting my work done. 

I definitely don't have any dark or scary thoughts that just pop up out of nowhere. I hope that's what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm not, like, giving you the wrong impression about how my brain works. I'm doing my best to stay focused and positive. Is that... does that answer your question okay?
Have you ever experienced any strange or unusual perceptions, like seeing or hearing things that others don’t, or having beliefs that other people might not share or understand?

Well, um... I really don't want you to think I'm, like, crazy or anything. I know it sounds a little weird, but... I mean, I'm sure it's just stress from work and school, right? 

But, um, sometimes... like if I'm just sitting alone at my desk trying to fix those ledgers, or if I'm walking home from class by myself... I'll hear this voice. It sounds like a man. And he'll say really normal, helpful things, actually! Like, 'check line seven' or 'you missed the sign.' It sounds so clear that I actually look around to see who's trying to help me, even when I'm totally alone. 

It's not scary or anything, I promise! It's almost like my brain is just working overtime to make sure I don't make any more mistakes. That's a pretty normal reaction to being stressed out, isn't it? I just... I hope telling you that doesn't make me sound like I'm losing my mind or something. It's really not a big deal.
How often do you hear that voice, and does it ever feel like it's coming from outside your head or from a real person who is actually there?

Um, well, it's not like it happens all the time or anything! Just, you know, sometimes. Like I said, mostly when I'm alone at my desk working, or sometimes when I'm walking home from class. 

And, um, yeah... it does sound like it's coming from outside my head. Like a real person. It's so clear that I'll physically turn around and look for the guy who's talking to me. But then there's nobody there. 

I know that probably sounds really bad, but I swear it's just helpful stuff! Like 'check line seven' or 'you missed the sign.' It's like a little study buddy or something. That's... that's not too crazy, right? I mean, the mind can play tricks on you when you're tired, I'm sure you hear about that all the time. I just want to make sure I'm not making it sound worse than it actually is.
Do you only hear the voice when you're feeling particularly stressed or tired, or have you noticed it happening even when you're feeling calm and rested?

Um, well... I guess I'd really like to say it's only when I'm super stressed out, because that would make the most sense, right? But... if I'm being completely honest—and I want to be honest so you can help me—it's happened at other times, too. 

There was this stretch, maybe for a few weeks, where things were actually pretty calm. I was getting normal sleep, I didn't feel all wired or stressed, just... regular. But I still heard the voice sometimes. And I still got kind of... pulled into looking for those number patterns in my ledgers. 

I really hope that doesn't mean something is seriously wrong with me. It's just a little quirk, I think? Even when I'm rested, my brain just likes to stay busy with the numbers and the helpful hints. That's... that's an okay thing to experience, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information without making it sound like I'm totally falling apart.
Have you ever had experiences like the voice you described happening when you weren't doing any work or school tasks—like when you're just relaxing or spending time with friends?

Um, no, not really. Like, if I'm just hanging out with my friends or, you know, watching a movie or something, I don't really notice it. 

It really is mostly just when I'm focused on something, or walking by myself. When I'm with other people, I guess my brain is just occupied with them, so it doesn't need to... chime in, I guess? 

So, I mean, that's a good sign, right? It means I can still relax and be normal around my friends. It's really just a minor thing that happens when I'm by myself. That makes it a lot less concerning, don't you think?
Have you ever had any experiences where you believed something strongly that others didn't seem to agree with or understand, even if they tried to tell you otherwise?

Um... well, there is this one thing, but it's probably just me overthinking, you know? Like, because I work with numbers all day, my brain just gets a little too invested in them. 

Sometimes... I know this sounds strange, but sometimes I get really convinced that certain invoice totals or account numbers, or even due dates, are... like, messages? About me. Like they're put there on purpose to see if I can figure out the pattern. 

I actually brought it up to my supervisor once, just to, you know, ask if she saw it too. And she showed me the original entries and explained how they were just normal, random numbers. And I nodded and agreed with her, of course! I didn't want her to think I was being difficult. But... even after she showed me, I still felt this really strong pull, like they were tracking whether I understood the code. 

I know that sounds a little weird when I say it out loud. But it's just an active imagination, right? I mean, bookkeeping can be so repetitive, it's normal to try and find a deeper meaning in it just to stay engaged. That's... that's not something to be super worried about, is it? I just want to make sure I'm doing okay.
How long have you been experiencing these voices and the strong feelings about numbers being messages?

Um... well, let me think. I guess... it's been going on for a little while now. Maybe around... eight months? Give or take? 

I know eight months sounds like a long time to be dealing with something like that, but honestly, it hasn't been a big deal every single day. Most of the time it's just in the background, you know? It's not like it's taking over my life or anything. 

I really hope eight months doesn't mean it's something permanent or, like, super serious. It's just a phase I'm going through while I adjust to the stress of work, right? I mean, a lot of people probably go through phases like this when they're young and starting out. Does that sound about right to you? I just really want to make sure I'm doing the right things to get past it.
Have you ever had any other beliefs that felt very real to you, even if others didn’t seem to understand or agree with them?

Um, no, not really. I mean, besides the thing with the numbers, I can't really think of anything else. 

I try to keep a pretty level head about most things, you know? I don't want you to think I'm just walking around believing all sorts of crazy stuff. I'm actually a really logical person most of the time—I have to be, for my job. 

So, yeah, it's really just that one specific thing with the invoices and accounts. That's good, right? That it's just isolated to that one area? I feel like that means I'm still mostly grounded in reality. That's what you want to hear, isn't it?
Have you ever had any other experiences where something felt very meaningful or significant to you in a way that others didn’t seem to understand, even if you didn’t talk about it much?

Um... well, honestly, it's really just what I mentioned before. About the numbers at work. I know we already talked about it, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record or make it seem like a bigger deal than it is. 

It's just... that feeling I get about the invoice totals and the due dates. Even after my supervisor sat down with me and showed me all the original entries, and I saw that they were just normal, everyday numbers... I still couldn't shake that feeling. Like, I still felt this tug, you know? Like they were put there to see if I could understand the pattern they were making about me. 

But really, that's the only thing. I don't have any other weird beliefs or anything like that. I promise I'm trying really hard to just focus on my work and do a good job. It's okay that I brought that up again, right? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the right way.
Have you ever had any other strong beliefs or feelings about things being meaningful or connected in a way that others didn't seem to understand, even if you didn't talk about it?

Um, no, really, there's nothing else like that. I know you've asked a couple of different ways, and I hope it's okay that my answer is still the same. 

I don't have any other strong feelings about things being connected or anything. It's just the numbers thing at work, like I said. I really try to keep my head down and just do my job, you know? I don't want to be the guy who's always reading into things or making things complicated. 

I'm sorry if I'm not giving you much else to go on... I just want to be honest and not make things up just to have something to say. That's the right thing to do, isn't it? I really am trying to be helpful here.
Have you ever had a time when these experiences—like hearing the voice or feeling like numbers are messages—lasted for a month or more without stopping?

Um... well, yeah, I guess they have. I mean, I don't want to make it sound like it's this constant, overwhelming thing every single second of the day, because I really do still get my work done. But... yeah, it's been going on for a while. 

If I really think about it, the voice and the... the feeling about the numbers... it's been about eight months now. I know that probably sounds like a long time, and I'm sorry I didn't mention it earlier. I just kept hoping it would kind of fade away on its own if I didn't make a big deal out of it. 

I've been trying really hard to just manage it myself so I don't bother anyone. Is it bad that it's been going on that long? I really hope you don't think worse of me for letting it go on for eight months without saying anything. I just wanted to handle it on my own, you know?
Have there been any periods where the voice and the feeling about numbers being messages happened almost every day for at least a month?

Um, yeah, I guess I'd have to say yes to that. Like I was just saying, it's... it's been about eight months now. And during that time, it's pretty much been an everyday thing. 

I mean, not all day, every day! It's not like I'm completely distracted or anything. I still get my spreadsheets done on time, and I'm always polite to my coworkers. It's just... you know, a little bit every day, I'll hear the voice or I'll get that feeling about the numbers. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm totally out of touch with reality. I know eight months of it happening every day sounds intense, but I promise I'm handling it okay. I mean, the fact that I can still do my job well means it's not too severe, right? I just want to be honest with you since you asked, but I hope you know I'm really trying my best.

Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs that felt very real to you, even if they weren’t based in reality, such as thinking that someone is watching you, sending you messages, or that events around you have special meaning for you specifically?

Um... well... I know we talked a little bit about the numbers thing already, but... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it does feel really real to me. Like, I know it sounds strange, and I'm sorry if it sounds crazy... but sometimes I get really convinced that certain invoice totals, or account numbers, or even due dates are, like, messages specifically about me. 

I don't talk about it much because I don't want to seem weird. Actually, one time my supervisor noticed I was staring at this one ledger for a long time, and he came over and showed me how they were just normal entries, just regular math. And I nodded and agreed with him, because I didn't want to be difficult or make him worry about my work. 

But... even after he showed me, I still felt like... like they were tracking whether I understood the pattern they were sending me. I just kept it to myself after that so I wouldn't bother him again. I really hope that doesn't make you think I'm doing a bad job at work. I still get all the accounts balanced, I promise. It's okay that I still feel that way sometimes, isn't it? As long as I keep it to myself and do my work?

Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs or experiences that felt very real to you, even if others might not understand or agree with them, outside of the feelings you've described about numbers and the voice?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I'm trying really hard to think if there's anything else, because I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information... but no, it's really just the voice and the feelings about the numbers. 

I haven't had anything else like that happen, like thinking people are watching me or anything else out of the ordinary. I hope it's okay that I don't have anything else to tell you for that one. I just don't want to make things up or waste your time, you know? 

Is it a good sign that it's only those two things? I really hope I'm answering your questions the right way. I'm just trying to be as helpful as I can.
Have you ever had any other experiences that felt very real to you, like seeing something that others don't or believing something strongly that isn't based in reality?

Um, no... no, I haven't. I mean, I know you just asked about other unusual beliefs, and I really want to make sure I'm not missing anything, but... I haven't seen anything that isn't there, or had any other strong beliefs like that. 

I really try to keep a level head, you know? I focus on my work, and I try to be a good employee. I haven't had any visions or anything scary like that. I hope that's okay, that my answer is still no? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to figure things out. I'm doing my best to be thorough, I promise.
